utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We have, well, two witnesses, a Bratunac Brigade military policeman and a Bosnian army intercept person. And if anyone has any time or energy left, we have a Dutchman who could fill in any time or we could save him for January. So we have perhaps some flexibility.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I see. Well, I have been just informed that on next Friday, the 19th of December, if we do not finish the witness, we have to sit in the afternoon from 2.00 to 7.00. I hope that nobody booked a ticket that night. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We only have two witnesses, Your Honour, in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I would prefer, Your Honour, to get as many witnesses done as possible. I think we can do it, only because, as I have indicated, I think that starting in January it would be -- I understand the Court wants to start on the 15th, but I think it would be wiser to work as much as we can next week and maybe have that entire week off for a couple of reasons, including, one, that I believe Mr. Stojanovic will be with a new co-counsel, and I'm sure he would appreciate the extra time for his co-counsel to come up to speed to be ready when we restart. So -- but in any event I certainly don't want to sit on Friday if we don't have to, but I'm prepared. I don't have a ticket and I'm not leaving town for a while, so it doesn't matter to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I think having said that, we'll resume next Tuesday, 2.15, in Courtroom I. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: at 6.29 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 16th day of December, 2003, at 2.15 p.m.
